nep̄eš takes any and the numeral ʾaḥaṯ takes one. The strongest competing reading is the reverse assignment: rule 15's licensing clause would make the ʾaḥaṯ standing on the noun what the determiner any renders, leaving nep̄eš its own word one, which would also put the head on the token realizing the lexeme and match the verse's own treatment of the second bare ʾaḥaṯ at s015. Kept as accepted because ʾaḥaṯ → one is the direct lexical match; the swap remains defensible.
ʿam hā-ʾāreṣ is rendered attributively as the common people (rules 28, 29), and the subject suffix on the infinitive is unrepresented, the ASV writing a bare gerund.
